method.source_hash: Sorted unique existing git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard paths: .rs/.sql/.json and Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock/rust-toolchain.toml; SHA-256 over path UTF-8, NUL, file bytes, NUL. Snapshot is captured before publishing the associated measurement; earlier reports may already exist.
method.saturation: 1/8/32 active runs and attempts; pending=2*C. Warmup=100 accepted runs. Each cycle accepts 3*C, verifies C blocked operations and exactly 3*C unfinished RunIds, rejects 3*C requests twice around a >=100 ms hold, then verifies one call and correct output per accepted run. At least 1000 measured runs and 30 seconds at full admission.
method.saturation_timing: Acceptance/rejection timed at each app.start; complete includes the controlled gate and scheduling; throughput is not maximum engine capacity.
method.release: 32 concurrent runs, 1 MiB payload, 64 terminal results maximum, retention=2000 ms. 100 warmup runs, ten cycles of 100 measured runs. Drop snapshots; wait 2050 ms after each cycle, verify not_found for every known ID, no unfinished runs, readiness true; sample RSS while the same runtime lives.
method.release_rss: ps -o rss= -p SELF_PID; KiB * 1024. Series retains warmup baseline, before-expiry and after-expiry RSS. Identity/latency metadata and one reusable input remain in the process; no payload snapshots kept by the harness.
method.peak_rss: Whole-process peak RSS in bytes from macOS /usr/bin/time -l
method.interpretation: Logical expiry does not require the allocator to return to startup RSS. A sustained trend or >15% post-warmup variation requires repetition/investigation.
method.passes_per_combination: One for saturation; memory release repeats ten cycles twice, extends to fifty, adds malloc counters, then adds final metadata-release probe; all observations retained.
method.revisions: 0: initial fixed ten-cycle harness. 1: optional release --cycles 10..100, unchanged default workload. 2: read-only macOS malloc counters outside timers, via target-specific dev-dependency libc 0.2.186. 3: final live-instance probe after dropping measurement IDs and latency vectors; compact report retained.
method.heap: macOS: malloc_zone_statistics(NULL, stats), all zones; live/reserved heap counters differ from RSS. No pressure relief or alternate allocator. Other platforms: null.
method.heap_peak: max_size_in_use was returned as zero on this host and is not used as a peak measurement; /usr/bin/time supplies peak RSS.
method.release_observation: Published release observations used a batch admission barrier before observing results. Static review found that early results may expire before the barrier completes. The current source observes start -> wait -> validate within each task. No full performance campaign was run on the corrected source; timings below belong to the recorded revisions.
method.release_retention: before_expiry_* means after executing a batch but before the explicit retention wait. With terminal_runs=64, it does not mean all 100 results remain retained. verified_expired_runs checks absence under count/age retention, not age-based expiry of every result.

analysis.interpretation: Initial RSS grows; the last 20 of 50 cycles vary below 0.3%. Every payload result expires and live allocations fall by about 192.5 MiB per cycle. After dropping IDs/timing vectors, live heap is about 1.88 MiB versus 1.66 MiB after warmup; compact report remains. This supports a local plateau with allocator reservation and instrument metadata, not a claim of universally bounded RSS or leak absence.
